name: epanet_orifice_line
description: A flange-tapped orifice plate of beta 0.5 between two reservoirs, as an EPANET GPV whose head-loss curve tabulates the plate's law: verifies ISO 5167-2's permanent loss with its Reynolds-number dependence and the line's flow and heads against EPANET 2.2.
source: WNTR 1.5.0 EpanetSimulator (EPANET 2.2.0); see tests/reference/generate_epanet_cases.py. D-W headloss, GPM INP units, accuracy 1e-5, headerror 1e-9 ft and flowchange 1e-12 gpm (EPANET reads both in the INP units, input1.c:595-596; WNTR writes them unconverted); viscosity VISCOS = 1.1e-5 ft2/s = 1.02193344e-6 m2/s (the project's custom fluid has the same nu; its density, 1000 kg/m3, does not affect the comparison because friction depends only on nu and a surface-pressure head p/(rho g) is converted with the same rho and g on both sides); solver run in 'swamee_jain' mode. Known EPANET biases, all far inside the 0.5% criterion: EPANET's head-loss coefficients use g = 32.2 ft/s2 = 9.81456 m/s2 against our 9.80665 (0.08% in head loss), its minor-loss constant is 0.02517 against the exact 1/(2g(pi/4)^2) = 0.0251730 in US units (0.012%), its GPM flow-unit constant GPMperCFS = 448.831 differs from the exact ft3/(gal/60) by -3.8e-07 (relative, in flow), and its results are float32 (about 1e-7 relative). Orifice plates: EPANET GPV between junctions at its ports' elevations, diameter of the inlet pipe, minor loss 0, whose HEADLOSS curve tabulates the plate's own law (element_laws.OrificeLaw) at 201 evenly spaced flows from 0 to the flow at which the plate alone would take the spread of the fixed heads (network_check.gpv_span), written by WNTR in gpm and ft with six decimals (checked against network_check.gpv_table); EPANET interpolates it linearly for either flow direction, so it solves the plate's Reynolds-number dependence itself, without its g or minor-loss constant. Expected orifice results from EPANET's flow and heads (derivations_orifice.orifice_result).
